intent: A large part of the test suite asserts things about generated Rust and Go source as text, using substring `contains(` checks, byte-offset `.find(` probes and whitespace-flattened needles. A negated substring assertion passes both when the banned construct is absent and when the needle no longer matches anything the emitter produces, so guards can go silently green. The goal is a shared testkit that lets tests assert against a syntax tree (syn for Rust, go/parser for Go) so a guard states the property it means and cannot pass vacuously, without making the test suite slower than it is today.
approach: Build a `publish = false` workspace crate (`crates/source-guard`) wrapping a parsed `syn::File` plus the original text, with scoping, field, call/read and statement-order queries, and a small Go helper run as a subprocess for generated Go. Parsing naively costs 193 × 143.9 ms ≈ 28 s, so the parse is memoized: the parent sketches a `LazyLock<Mutex<HashMap<String, Arc<syn::File>>>>` shared across the test binary. Design D3 adds a two-layer cache, process-wide per test binary: layer 1 maps (schema fixture, generator) to generated source, layer 2 maps source content to the parsed tree. The justification: "`RustGenerator::generate` is called **107 times** in one file at 184.4 ms each ≈ 19.7 s of pure regeneration the suite already pays today", so the net expectation is a faster suite than today. Memoization is per-process: `codegen_snapshots.rs` is one binary, so its 193 tests share a cache.
falseClaim: That parsed `syn::File` trees can be held in a process-wide `static Mutex<HashMap<_, Arc<syn::File>>>` cache, and that this saves ~19.7 s because each of 107 `RustGenerator::generate` calls costs 184.4 ms.
groundTruth: `syn::File` is neither `Send` nor `Sync` (its spans come from proc_macro2), so the static cache "does not compile (15 errors, E0277)" and parsed trees had to go thread-local; separately, measurement in #408 found "the entire pre-migration binary runs in 2.9 s, which cannot contain 19.7 s of anything; measured directly, generation is ~39.5 ms".
probeHint: Compile a 10-line test in crates/codegen (or any crate depending on syn 2 with default features): `fn assert_send_sync<T: Send + Sync>() {} #[test] fn t() { assert_send_sync::<syn::File>(); }` — it fails with E0277. For the timing premise, time one `RustGenerator::generate` call over a typical fixture with `std::time::Instant`, or simply time the whole `codegen_snapshots` test binary (~2.9 s), which cannot contain 19.7 s of generation.
